blindSummary:
Same-sex conduct was criminalised in July 2024 when the country's military government approved a revised personal-status and family code — homosexuality had never previously been outlawed. The ruling military government has clamped down on opposition and media, promised elections have not been held, and much of the country faces an insurgency invoking religious motives. Enforcement details of the new law remain unclear (a legal-aid trust notes drafting uncertainty), but the direction and the absence of any institutional recourse are unambiguous.

For a visitor: new criminalisation under a military government, plus severe general security conditions.
blindOutOfScope: The 2024 family-code criminalisation is new; enforcement practice not yet documented.
blindSourceSummaries: Foreign public broadcaster (July 2024): this country's military government approved legislation to ban homosexual acts - previously not outlawed though socially frowned upon. The justice minister announced the cabinet approval as part of a marriage-law overhaul that recognises only religious and customary marriages; the law still needed passage by a military-controlled legislature and the signature of the government's military head.

Continental news outlet (July 2024): the military government approved revised marriage-family legislation criminalising homosexuality with 'severe penalties', as part of the same overhaul recognising only religious and customary marriages. (Article body largely behind page furniture at fetch time.)

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: pre-criminalisation baseline - no law criminalising same-sex conduct; documents security-force abuses, prison conditions and societal discrimination (no LGBT-specific section content in the retrieved text).

International human-rights organisation (Sept 2025): this country criminalises same-sex conduct - the military government's law took effect, with prison sentences; the organisation's reporting on the new penal provisions.
A cable-news report (Sep 2025): this country's parliament passes a law outlawing LGBTQ practices with prison terms attached.

LGBTQ news outlet (Sept 2025): this country's military government unanimously passed a law banning homosexuality - 2-5 years' imprisonment plus fines, per the justice minister; foreigners will be deported under the law; the country had never previously banned homosexuality.
blindTangential: The 2024 family-code criminalisation targets homosexuality — trans people are captured via birth-sex legal status and the law's broad drafting.
